posts.summary: As you might have heard recently, widespread system outages highlighted in F/OSS Comics #13: BSD Unix, Part 3 – The Beginning of BSD Unix raised questions about OS stability. Let's learn about this: modern CPUs enforce hardware privilege levels where user applications run in restricted Ring 3 without direct hardware access, while the OS kernel operates in privileged Ring 0. A crash in Ring 3 terminates only that app, but an unhandled fault in Ring 0 triggers a full system crash (BSOD or Kernel Panic).

Let's learn about this: instead of activating all billions of parameters for every single token, MoE systems use a lightweight Router Gate to dynamically dispatch each token to only top-k expert subnetworks, drastically slashing computation while maintaining high representation capacity.
key_points: Underlying Mechanism: Solves critical performance or reliability constraints without brute-force hardware overhead.

# Sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) Routing
import torch
def moe_routing(tokens, router_weights, top_k=2):
    logits = torch.matmul(tokens, router_weights) # [batch, num_experts]
    top_weights, top_indices = torch.topk(torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1), top_k)
    return top_weights, top_indices # Send tokens only to selected experts

posts.title: Linear Attention Mechanisms in Transformers
posts.subtitle: Achieving constant-memory recurrent state updates to eliminate the quadratic KV cache bottleneck
posts.summary: As you might have heard recently, Cerebras demonstrated how it deploys trillion-parameter models like Kimi K3 across dozens of wafer-scale chips by exploiting hybrid linear-attention layers that require zero KV cache. But what actually is *Linear Attention*? Let's learn about this: Standard softmax attention computes quadratic token-to-token interactions and stores every past Key and Value tensor in memory, causing memory usage to surge linearly with context length. Linear attention avoids the non-linear softmax operation by using kernel feature maps, allowing matrix multiplications to be reordered via the associative property. This collapses historical context into a fixed-size recurrent memory tensor, enabling O(1) inference memory per token regardless of context length.
key_points: Softmax Bottleneck: Standard attention evaluates softmax(Q @ K.T) @ V, where the row-wise softmax couples Q and K, preventing reordering and mandating O(N) sequence KV cache storage.

Associative Kernel Decomposition: By replacing softmax with non-negative kernel feature maps phi(x), attention simplifies to phi(Q) @ (phi(K).T @ V), enabling the calculation of (phi(K).T @ V) first as a constant-sized state matrix S.

Constant-Memory Recurrence: During autoregressive generation, new tokens update the state matrix via S_t = S_{t-1} + phi(k_t).T @ v_t in O(d^2) compute and O(1) memory, eliminating multi-gigabyte KV caches for 100k+ token sequences.
posts.code_snippet:
def linear_attention_step(q_t, k_t, v_t, s_prev):
    # Apply kernel feature map (ELU + 1) to ensure non-negativity
    phi_q = torch.nn.functional.elu(q_t) + 1.0  # Shape: (1, d_k)
    phi_k = torch.nn.functional.elu(k_t) + 1.0  # Shape: (1, d_k)
    # Recurrent accumulation: S_t = S_{t-1} + phi(k_t)^T @ v_t
    s_curr = s_prev + torch.matmul(phi_k.T, v_t)  # Fixed shape: (d_k, d_v)
    # Decode token in O(1) memory without caching token history
    out = torch.matmul(phi_q, s_curr)
    return out, s_curr

complexity.time_or_memory: O(1) memory per decoding step; O(N) linear time and memory across sequence length N
complexity.paradigm: Kernel Feature Mapping & Associative Matrix Reordering

posts.interview_tip: When asked about scaling Transformers to ultra-long contexts in systems interviews, contrast Softmax Attention's O(N^2) training and O(N) KV-cache inference against Linear Attention / State Space Models (Mamba, RWKV) which leverage the associative property (A @ B) @ C = A @ (B @ C) to reduce KV cache to a fixed-size state.

posts.subtitle: How large-scale distributed systems achieve sub-millisecond reads
posts.summary: Caching places high-frequency data in lightning-fast in-memory stores (like Redis or Memcached) to prevent exhausting your primary database.

key_points: Structure: Self-balancing multi-way search tree where leaf nodes form a doubly linked list.
Clustered vs Non-Clustered: Clustered determines physical row storage order (Primary Key). Non-clustered stores indexed columns with pointers to the data rows.
Composite Index: An index on (user_id, created_at) must follow the Leftmost Prefix Rule to be utilized.

posts.title: Process vs Thread Explained Visually
posts.subtitle: The #1 favorite question asked in university exams & technical rounds
posts.summary: A Process is an executing program with its own dedicated memory space, whereas a Thread is a lightweight unit of execution within that process.
key_points: Memory Isolation: Processes have independent virtual address spaces (Stack, Heap, Code). If one process crashes, others are unaffected.
Shared Memory: Threads within the same process share the Heap and Data segments, but have their own private Registers and Stack.
Context Switching: Thread switching is significantly faster than process switching because MMU page tables do not need to be flushed.
IPC: Processes communicate via Inter-Process Communication (Pipes, Sockets, Shared Memory). Threads communicate directly through shared memory variables.

t1.start()

# Multi-processing: bypasses Python GIL for CPU-bound tasks
p1 = Process(target=heavy_math_computation)
p1.start()
